bootstrap.allowedToolNames: sorted unique UTF-8 byte order; maxItems=32; each matches ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$
bootstrap.canonical: strict duplicate-key rejection; bounded object; UTF-8 JSON
bootstrap.handshakeDeadline: 5 seconds; absent, malformed, or unsupported handshake terminates harness and refuses upstream with invalid_protocol/unsupported_version

chatAccounting.decrement: after local validation succeeds, atomically reserve one slot immediately before upstream I/O; a reserved attempt consumes exactly one forever
chatAccounting.emission: pre-reservation failure consumes zero and emits none; every post-reservation terminal consumes exactly one and emits exactly one delegation provider-attempt stage
chatAccounting.replay: replayed requestId is rejected before reservation and consumes no request
chatAccounting.remainingRequests: broker session state returned by handshake only; never carried in relayed SSE

protocol.distinctRequestIds: at most 8 accepted reservations per session; every accepted requestId is unique within that session

grant.chat: provider and model must equal grant; chat tool names must be a subset
grant.generated: once from task/run inputs by kernel
grant.model: exact case-sensitive value matching bootstrap model and ^[A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{1,256}$
grant.toolNames: exact case-sensitive values matching ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$, maxItems=32, sorted unique by UTF-8 bytes

httpAdmission.acceptLoop: bounded non-blocking accept loop; refuse further accepts while 64 unauthenticated connections are pending
httpAdmission.framing: Content-Length is required for requests with a body; Transfer-Encoding/chunked, Content-Length plus Transfer-Encoding, duplicate Content-Length, and conflicting Content-Length values are rejected
httpAdmission.json: strict duplicate-key rejection before authentication or body dispatch
httpAdmission.providerSlot: unauthenticated header/body admission is completed before authentication, validation, and the single provider-attempt slot reservation; partial unauthenticated clients cannot consume that slot
httpAdmission.implementation: bounded parser and socket deadlines; do not rely on undocumented http.server knobs
httpAdmission.rationale: 16 KiB headers, 100 fields, and 8 KiB request lines stay below common stdlib line limits while bounding unauthenticated memory and header abuse; five seconds matches the handshake deadline
httpAdmission.pendingRationale: 64 pending unauthenticated connections bound pre-auth resource use; a local process can still occupy the pending pool for up to the read deadline and deny the legitimate harness admission — a bounded local availability residual (the provider slot itself is never consumed)
httpAdmission.availabilityResidual: bounded local admission DoS remains possible; owner-accepted availability trade-off, recorded with the other known limits
httpAdmission.contentLengthRationale: rejecting a declared body above maxRequestBytes at admission avoids allocating or reading an oversized unauthenticated request

httpSse.countBefore: decode, parse, or write; includes delimiters, comments, BOM, DONE, and offending bytes
httpSse.done: only a dispatched event whose assembled data is exactly [DONE]; terminal event relayed unchanged
httpSse.eof: EOF before DONE, invalid UTF-8, malformed framing, line/event/body limit => upstream_protocol
httpSse.post200Failure: close downstream without synthetic SSE or status after downstream 200 is committed; tracing remains verdict-neutral
httpSse.relay: preserve each complete valid event original bytes exactly; no JSON rewriting

logging.broker: no independent broker log; the kernel-owned reservation ledger is separate from ADR-031 tracing
logging.harness: must not emit delegation stage events

audit.emitter: exactly one ADR-031 emitter invocation per reserved attempt
audit.materialization: materialized only when tracing is enabled; tracing disabled is verdict-neutral and emits nothing
audit.authority: observability event only; not an authoritative durable audit

reservationLedger.identity: each row carries the secret-free correlation fields taskId, session, requestId (when applicable), provider, model, and attemptCorrelationId = sha256 over canonical JSON {taskId, session, requestId} with sorted keys and compact separators; no secret material
reservationLedger.stageEventLinkage: the single ADR-031 provider_attempt stage event carries attemptCorrelationId as its non-null subject_digest; ledger rows and the stage event join on attemptCorrelationId; no new trace-schema field is introduced
reservationLedger.crashRecovery: at broker start, a reserved row without a terminal row is reconciled by appending a terminal row with outcome internal and marker reconciled_after_restart before any new reservation is accepted; a reconciliation pass applies the same rule to reserved rows older than timeoutSeconds + 60 seconds without a terminal row
reservationLedger.fields: secret-free row identity, outcome code on terminal row, and hash-chain link
reservationLedger.residual: does not detect rollback or truncation; characterized in SLICE-056

providerAttempt.emitter: kernel broker exactly once per reserved attempt; harness never emits
providerAttempt.subjectDigest: non-null; equals attemptCorrelationId = sha256 over canonical JSON {taskId, session, requestId} with sorted keys and compact separators

logging.schemaEvolution: issue #43 owns the additive schema.py registry entry and its schema contract tests; this ADR and fixture define the valid event instance

protocol.name: ranex-delegated-provider
protocol.persistence: no prompts or outputs; exactly two secret-free hash-chained reservation ledger rows per reserved attempt

policy.chatProvider: if omitted, use the authenticated session provider; if present, it must equal the session provider
policy.chatTools: function.name set must be subset of handshake tools

security.scope: accidental secret non-propagation and credential hygiene across the harness process boundary; not isolation against an adversarial same-UID harness
security.sameUidResidual: a same-UID adversary may ptrace-attach or read /proc/<pid>/ where permitted and extract the raw key; O_CLOEXEC, FD discipline, and capability bounds do not address process-memory inspection
security.optionalDeploymentHardening: separate UID, yama ptrace_scope, and hidepid proc mounts are optional deployment preconditions left to the owner; they are not protocol requirements

preStreamHttpStatus.preStream: return bounded generic JSON {error,message}; never leak upstream body
preStreamHttpStatus.post200: after downstream 200 headers commit, close downstream without synthetic SSE or status; no pre-stream status is returned and the observability event is not a durable audit

protocol.schemaValidation: handshake/chat provider/model/tools schemas are structurally permissive on purpose so authoritative validation+policy returns stable provider_not_allowed/model_not_allowed/tool_not_allowed; bootstrap+grant carry stricter immutable shapes

transport.bootstrap: one bounded canonical JSON object on an O_CLOEXEC pipe at exact FD 3
transport.brokerTransport: direct TLS through a verified HTTP stack
transport.capability: random capability in bootstrap, then authenticated handshake
transport.childEnvironment: explicit allowlist; excludes raw key and credential-pattern variables
transport.fd3CloseAll: kernel reads and closes its ingress FD 3; after that it creates a distinct child pipe whose read end is mapped to harness FD 3 and whose bytes are capability bootstrap only; the descriptor number is reused across process boundaries, never the bytes
transport.fd3SelfAlias: source read fd == 3 is repaired before posix_spawn by CLOEXEC duplication to fd >=4; no self-DUP2 close-order ambiguity
transport.harnessEntry: reads bounded capability bootstrap from child FD 3 at earliest entrypoint, validates, closes FD 3 immediately after the bounded read and before command/session/model/children
transport.harnessStorage: bounded in-memory only under non-adversarial broker dataflow (see protocol.security.sameUidResidual)
transport.httpStack: Python stdlib http.client HTTPSConnection directly to openrouter.ai:443 with normal certificate and hostname verification; no custom HTTP or TLS replacement

upstreamRequest.connection: direct HTTPSConnection to openrouter.ai:443; no proxy, tunnel, or configurable endpoint
upstreamRequest.authorization: broker constructs Authorization internally from the kernel-only raw key
upstreamRequest.forwarded: harness cannot supply or forward Authorization, custom headers, proxy settings, endpoint, transport, TLS, or debug options

transport.legacyRefusal: any harness absent/malformed/unsupported FD3 bootstrap, non-FD3 bootstrap, or handshake not authenticated within 5 seconds is terminated/refused as invalid_protocol or unsupported_version before upstream; no raw-key fallback or legacy CLI
transport.rawKeyIngress: kernel receives the raw provider key only through an inherited FD/pipe owned by the kernel process under non-adversarial broker dataflow (see protocol.security.sameUidResidual)
rawKeyProhibited: request bodies; under non-adversarial broker dataflow (see protocol.security.sameUidResidual)
transport.rawKeyResidency: kernel/broker memory only under non-adversarial broker dataflow (see protocol.security.sameUidResidual)
transport.spawn: kernel reads and closes its inherited raw-key ingress FD; it then creates a distinct O_CLOEXEC child pipe, maps only the capability bootstrap read end to harness FD 3, closes the source/original and unrelated descriptors using the verified close-all strategy, then setsid
transport.sseValidator: in-repository bounded frame validator implementing exactly the frozen WHATWG-compatible grammar; no custom TLS/HTTP replacement

requestId.terminalCharacters: must be one of AQgw; any other final character is invalid_request

session.oracle: stable error code and generic message only; disclose no session existence or capability details

protocol.preDownstreamNormalization: ordered states, each with exactly one non-overlapping named code: DNS failure → upstream_dns; TCP connect failure → upstream_connect; TLS failure → upstream_tls; upstream disconnect or transport error before COMPLETE valid response headers → upstream_http; a complete upstream response (classification at status line and headers, before any body) with a 3xx redirect status → redirect_refused (redirects are refused, never followed); any other non-200 status → upstream_http; a 200 response with missing, malformed, or non-text/event-stream Content-Type (media-type parameters permitted per RFC 9110) → upstream_protocol; all classified before downstream commitment (downstream receives the mapped 502 pre-stream status, never the upstream body); after valid 200 text/event-stream response headers are received and the downstream 200 is committed, EOF before the SSE DONE sentinel or any other upstream protocol violation → upstream_protocol with post-200 close-downstream semantics (no synthetic status); client_cancelled has no downstream status because downstream is already gone and its reservation is consumed
protocol.terminalPrecedence: the terminal outcome is the first terminal condition the broker observes; if a downstream client close and an upstream failure are observed in the same event-loop iteration, client_cancelled takes precedence

chatResponse.description: Opaque raw SSE relay; each event is forwarded without constraining model-specific response structure.

chat.meaning: broker state observation; never an SSE body

vectorSemantics.independence: each vector is evaluated from its declared state; replay vectors reuse only their declared key
vectorSemantics.syntaxVector: zero-byte deterministic encodings pin syntax only; runtime randomness is implementation-tested

vectors.portSemantics: non-normative allocated-port example; implementation binds an OS-assigned port in the schema range

expected.sse: opaque relay; not a literal vector body
opaque relay; not a literal vector body
